body.x: The Future Innovation Tech Expo 2026 (FIX 2026) officially concluded on Saturday, October 24, at EXCO in Daegu, marking its most expansive edition to date after welcoming more than 117,000 attendees over its four-day run. Organized under the banner “AI, Beyond Tech into Reality,” the cross-industry exhibition utilized all available halls across EXCO, hosting 588 exhibiting companies across 2,000 booths. International participation expanded significantly, with overseas companies accounting for 27.5% (162 exhibitors), highlighted by the Korean debut of the full-scale ‘VoloCity’ urban air mobility (UAM) aircraft by Germany’s Volocopter alongside software and artificial intelligence delegations from 30 leading ASEAN technology firms.

The exhibition demonstrated the accelerating convergence of physical AI, autonomous transport, and digital infrastructure across four specialized sectors: future mobility, robotics, ICT, and startups. In the East Wing’s mobility hall, Hyundai Motor Company presented its ATRIA AI and Pleos software architectures alongside GMTCK’s Super Cruise driver assistance platform. Regional tier-one automotive suppliers demonstrated advanced industrial transformation, with SL Corporation highlighting robot-automated manufacturing processes, Sambo Motors displaying its scaled B-33X UAM airframe and multipurpose drones, and PHC exhibiting high-output inverters and robotic actuators. Global automakers, including Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, Zeekr, and BYD, showcased production electric vehicles, while Volocopter’s interactive VoloCity cockpit-boarding simulations sustained public engagement throughout the event.

body.cap: A bird's eye view on the ROBEX hall | Photo provided by Daegu Metropolitan City

body.x: The West Wing featured landmark participation from Korea’s industrial robotics leaders, with HD Hyundai Robotics and Doosan Robotics making their official FIX debuts. HD Hyundai Robotics demonstrated manufacturing automation workflows with its next-generation HDC35-18 collaborative robot and new dual-arm units, while Doosan Robotics exhibited industrial productivity systems anchored by its CES Best of Innovation Award-winning Scan&Go platform. In the ICT hall, practical applications of AI were showcased through Geobot’s autonomous sinkhole-exploration robot, AIRC’s PnGO unmanned robotic convenience store platform, and Farmity’s FIRA Pose spatial recognition system, validating AI’s role in municipal safety, retail automation, and preventative healthcare.

The startup vertical brought together 91 global partners from 12 countries to foster international venture capital linkage, while 30 high-growth Korean ventures exhibited at the Startup Arena. A cornerstone of the startup ecosystem was the specialized corporate zone operated by the Daegu Center for Creative Economy & Innovation (DCCEI, CEO Han In-kook), which showcased 14 regional deep-tech companies backed by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ Startup City Project.

body.cap: A scene from the stage event in the ITCE hall | Photo provided by Daegu Metropolitan City

body.x: Operating under a policy to decentralize capital from the Seoul capital area, DCCEI deployed tailored commercialization funding of up to KRW 400 million for emerging future tech and KRW 250 million for manufacturing to support ventures including Nuvinda, Yellosis, A.Cure, Zio Robot, EROP, AIEEV, LearningVision, FutureDrive, WPosition, AIRS, UNIVA, RootLab, Muaheng, and TheSunHan. During media sessions led by Kijung Ju, Director of DCCEI’s Startup City Division, participating founders pitched directly to visiting international journalists, spotlighting Nuvinda’s 120Nm-class high back-drivability actuator for humanoid robots, TheSunHan’s YAK on-premises AI computing infrastructure, AIEEV’s Private Air Cloud enterprise agent platform, and LearningVision’s composite visual AI battery inspection system.

Academic and technical discourse was anchored by the FIX 2026 Conference, which convened 61 industry executives and scholars from 14 countries. Keynote addresses were delivered by Brian McMurray, President of GMTCK; Professor Kyu-Jin Cho of Seoul National University; Francesco Ferro, CEO of PAL Robotics; and Professor Xiaoxiao Li of the Vector AI Institute, complemented by a public lecture on applied AI by science communicator Jaehyeok Kim (Orbit) of UnrealScience.

body.x: International press engagement and industry evaluation were integrated into two major award programs. The FIX Innovation Awards ceremony, held on October 22 with Daegu Vice Mayor for Administrative Affairs Jung-ki Kim, recognized 31 companies selected from a competitive field of 209 applicants. Top honors were awarded to nine category champions: ONEPREDICT, SWM, PERSEUS, and HJWAVE in future mobility; Tesollo and AeiROBOT in robotics; and CENS, WACE, and POTATONET in AI/ICT. That afternoon, official media partner AVING News co-hosted the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day, where a 13-member international press delegation from 13 news organizations held technical briefings with the category winners.

body.cap: A group photo of winners and award presenters, including Daegu Mayor Kyungho Choo, of the FIX Innovation Awards 2026 | Photo provided by Daegu Metropolitan City

body.x: On October 23, global press coverage culminated in the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards ceremony held at the FIX TV Zone under the banner of ‘Startup City Daegu’, opened by Mi-jung Kim, Team Leader of Daegu’s Future Mobility Division. Ten international media outlets each selected three standout enterprises, highlighting 30 market-ready leaders. Honors were conferred by Le Café du Geek (BEYLESS, Brain-Life Link, TESOLLO), Clipset (TOFF MOBILITY, WAVUS, PYUNGHWA HOLDINGS), Ubergizmo (Doosan Robotics, DOGU Robotics, Rezbin Waste Technology), Otaku Soken (MIRAEROBOT, HD Hyundai Robotics, U&S Networks), DIGITIMES (LVIS Korea, OPTOELEC, KAR Co., Ltd.), ChinaByte (YHDATABASE, ORGO, NRT Sensors), ET Manufacturing (BRATO, D,RIVE, AeiROBOT), VietnamPlus (Farmity, JINMYUNG I&C, iM Robotics), Pokde.net (STM Corporation, GEOBOT, Intellectus Corp.), and AVING USA (MOBILTECH, AIRC Inc., YOUNG HYUN ROBOTICS). Accepting the honor, Jinhyo Kim, Founder and CEO of DOGU Robotics, noted that recognition by Silicon Valley-based Ubergizmo will support the company’s US expansion via its new San Jose office.

body.cap: Group photo of media outlets who judged for the Best of FIX 2026 Global Media Awards | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Commercial dealmaking across the four-day event generated substantial business outcomes, with KOTRA-arranged international export consultations reaching USD 353 million and domestic procurement sessions with conglomerates such as SK Hynix and HD Hyundai Heavy Industries recording KRW 32 billion, yielding a total consultation volume of approximately KRW 508.6 billion. Daegu Metropolitan City also operated cultural tourism programs for visiting delegates, including night tours of 83 Tower and visits to the Daegu International Opera Festival. Mayor Kyung-ho Choo stated that FIX 2026 achieved significant qualitative advancement as an international innovation showcase, affirming that the city will continue leveraging this multi-sector platform to accelerate industrial AI adoption and expand global business opportunities.
